## 1. Company Overview & Core Expertise

Jee Engineers is a premier machinery manufacturing company based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India. Specializing in sustainable building equipment, Jee Engineers designs and manufactures high-performance Fly Ash Brick Making Machines, Concrete Block Machines, Hydraulic Presses, Pan Mixers, Conveyor Systems, and Custom Industrial Moulds.

Our machinery enables entrepreneurs and construction enterprises to produce high-density, eco-friendly fly ash bricks that conform to Indian Standards (IS 12894:2001) and global quality benchmarks.

---

## 2. Product Portfolio & Machinery Lineup

### 2.1 Manual & Semi-Automatic Fly Ash Brick Machines
- **Target User**: Small-scale enterprises, start-ups, and regional building material suppliers.
- **Features**: Sturdy structural design, manual or semi-automated feeder and ejection mechanism, cost-effective initial investment.
- **Productivity**: 1,000 to 4,000 bricks per 8-hour shift.
- **Power Requirement**: 7.5 HP to 15 HP depending on model.

### 2.2 Hydraulic Press Fly Ash Brick Machines
- **Target User**: Medium to large production plants requiring high compressive strength.
- **Technology**: High-tonnage hydraulic compression (30 to 100+ tons) ensuring uniform compaction, sharp edges, and zero thermal cracking.
- **Productivity**: 4,000 to 10,000 bricks per shift.
- **Benefits**: Superior density, precise brick dimensions, consistent quality output.

### 2.3 Fully Automatic Fly Ash Brick Plants
- **Target User**: Commercial manufacturers and high-volume industrial projects.
- **Components**:
  - Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) touch-screen panel for automated operations.
  - Automatic batching and pan mixer system (300 kg to 1000 kg capacity).
  - Hydraulic pressing station with automatic feeder box.
  - Automatic stacker system and pallet conveyor.
- **Productivity**: 10,000 to 25,000+ bricks per 8-hour shift.

### 2.4 Paver Block & Concrete Block Machinery
- Interchangeable custom moulds for manufacturing interlocking pavers, zig-zag blocks, I-shape pavers, solid concrete blocks, and hollow blocks.

## 3. Fly Ash Bricks vs Red Clay Bricks Comparison

| Feature | Fly Ash Bricks | Red Clay Bricks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Compressive Strength** | 7.5 to 12 N/mm² (High) | 3.5 to 5 N/mm² (Moderate/Varies) |
| **Water Absorption** | 6% - 12% (Low absorption) | 15% - 20% (High absorption) |
| **Shape & Dimensional Uniformity** | Exact uniform rectangular shape, smooth edges | Irregular shapes, uneven surfaces |
| **Mortar Consumption** | Saves up to 20-30% joint mortar | Higher mortar required due to uneven surface |
| **Plaster Requirement** | Minimal plaster coating needed | Thicker plaster required |
| **Environmental Impact** | Eco-friendly; utilizes industrial waste (fly ash) | Topsoil depletion; high CO2 emissions |
| **Weight** | ~2.6 - 3.2 kg (Lighter structure load) | ~3.5 - 4.2 kg (Heavier load) |
| **Thermal & Acoustic Insulation** | Superior thermal insulation | Moderate thermal performance |

---

## 4. Manufacturing Process & Recommended Mix Ratios

### 4.1 Raw Materials
1. **Fly Ash** (60% - 70%): Industrial byproduct from thermal power plants.
2. **Sand / Stone Dust / Quarry Dust** (20% - 30%): Fine aggregate binder and matrix filler.
3. **Lime / Cement** (8% - 12%): Binding agent (Hydrated lime or OPC cement).
4. **Gypsum** (3% - 5%): Accelerates early setting and strength accumulation.

### 4.2 Step-by-Step Manufacturing Workflow
1. **Raw Material Batching**: Weighed proportioning of fly ash, quarry dust, lime/cement, and gypsum.
2. **Pan Mixing**: Homogeneous dry and wet mixing with water in an industrial pan mixer for 3 to 5 minutes.
3. **Feeder Conveying**: Mixed material is conveyed into the feeder hopper of the brick press.
4. **Hydraulic / Vibro Compaction**: Material is fed into heavy-duty moulds and compressed under high hydraulic pressure (up to 100 tons).
5. **Ejection & Palletizing**: Formed bricks are ejected onto wooden/PVC pallets.
6. **Water Curing**: Bricks are water-cured for 7 to 14 days to attain maximum compressive strength.

---

## 5. Starting a Fly Ash Brick Business & Plant Setup

### 5.1 Land & Infrastructure Requirements
- **Total Area Needed**: 0.5 to 1.5 acres (includes machinery footprint, raw material yard, and brick curing area).
- **Power Connection**: 15 HP to 50 HP 3-Phase commercial electrical connection.
- **Water Supply**: Continuous water source for mixing and daily curing operations (approx. 3,000 - 10,000 liters/day).

### 5.2 Business Licensing & Compliance
- Business Registration (Proprietorship / LLP / Pvt Ltd)
- GST Registration
- Factory License / Trade License
- State Pollution Control Board (NOC / Consent to Establish)
- MSME / Udyam Registration (for government subsidy access)

### 5.3 Economic & ROI Outlook
- Fly ash brick production offers attractive profit margins due to abundant raw material availability near power plants and rising demand for eco-friendly construction materials.
- Payback period typically ranges from 12 to 24 months depending on capacity utilization.

## 6. Maintenance & Troubleshooting Best Practices

### 6.1 Daily & Weekly Maintenance Checklist
- **Hydraulic Oil Level**: Check hydraulic fluid reservoir and oil cleanliness daily.
- **Lubrication**: Grease all moving joints, guide pins, and feeder slides every 8 operational hours.
- **Pan Mixer Inspection**: Clean pan mixer blades and liners to prevent hardened concrete buildup.
- **Filter Cleaning**: Inspect air breather filters and hydraulic oil suction filters monthly.

### 6.2 Troubleshooting Diagnostics
- **Low Compression Pressure**: Check hydraulic relief valve settings, inspect cylinder seals, and verify oil viscosity.
- **Cracks in Ejected Bricks**: Adjust moisture content in raw mix (too dry or too wet), verify mold alignment, and check ejection speed.
- **Uneven Brick Thickness**: Clean feeder box distribution plate and recalibrate hydraulic stroke limiters.
